1. By way of the present application under Section 12 of the Protection of  Women From Domestic Violence Act, 2005, Smt. Lalita (hereinafter referred to  as "the aggrieved'') has sought various reliefs against her husband and  parents in law (hereinafter referred as "the respondents") including Protection  CC No: 13/1/15 Lalita v Pawan & Ors. Page 1  order under Section 18, Residence Order under Section 19, Monetary relief  under Section 20, Compensation order under section 22 of the Act.

As per the aggrieved she married the respondent no.1 on 13.03.2013 at  Kanyadan Mahadan Vivah Sammelan, Gandhi Harijan Vidyalaya, Dakshinpuri, 
Dr. Ambedkar Nagar as per Hindu rites and customs in which several gifts were  given to the parties and after her marriage she stayed with the respondents.

sentences.text: The aggrieved states that in the month of April, 2013, the respondents  started taunting her for insufficient dowry including less gifts regarding the less  gifts/articles/ cash and Marriage Video etc. and when she expressed inability of  her parents to fulfill their demands, they abused her and warned her to go to her  parent's house with her luggage and also took all her jewellery.

She has stated  that she was subjected to comments and taunts in all her daily activities e.g. 
eating, sitting, sleeping etc. caused her mental harassment.

4. She has further stated that one day, the respondents pressurized her to  arrange a two wheeler vehicle for the respondent no.1 and cash amount Rs. 1  lakh from her parents and if she did not do so she will be thrown out and
when  she objected she was beaten by them.

She has further stated that since her  marriage, she has been subjected to regular abuse and beatings by respondent  no.1 who also pressurize her to work for living and also threatened to kill her if  she disclosed about their torture to anybody including the neighbours or her  parents.
5.

She has also stated that after marriage she came to know ab respondent no.1 being a habitual drunker with the habit of eating Gutka and  CC No: 13/1/15 Lalita v Pawan & Ors. Page 2 of 1  that he used to spend his money on drinking and gambling and also beat her  when she objected.

She has further stated that respondent no. 1 used to snatch  all her money and also pressurized her to fulfill their demands of Rupees One  Lakh in cash and two wheeler vehicle and upon her inability threatened to kill  her and threw her out of the house.
She has further stated on 09.10.2013, she

made a complaint at Mahila Panchayat where the respondents were called and  matter was compromised and she was sent back with the respondents on their  assurance of keeping her happy without further harassment

but despite being  brought back on 18.11.2013, the respondents repeated their behaviour and on  Smt. Lalita vs Sh. Pawan Kumar on 7 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163182144/
2 10.05.2015 when the respondent no.1 tried to strangle her, respondent  (mother in law) caught hold of her hands and respondent no.2 (father in law), 
brother in law and sister in law also helped and respondent no.1 assaulted her  with "Thapki" (wooden bat) on her head and back causing her injuries.

sentences.text: She left  the matrimonial house on 12.05.2014 and got an MLC done.

6. She has stated that since 12.05.2014, she has been living at the house of  her parents, does not have any source of income, is dependent on her parents, 
with three sisters and her father being the only earning member whereas the  respondents no.1 has own house and earns more than Rs. 15,000/ per month  from private job. 
7.
She has also stated that she made complaint to the CAW Cel September, 2014 upon which FIR no. 664/14 was registered at PS San Vihar.

She has also stated that she suffered a miscarriage due to beatings by  respondents who has also threatened to kill her and kidnap her younger sisters  CC No: 13/1/15 Lalita v Pawan & Ors. Page 3 o  if she makes a complaint.

she is frightened

. 
8. The aggrieved has stated that the respondents have refused to maintain  her nor have given her any financial security and that all her jewellery and  stridhen, gifts and all other household articles given by the family, friends and  relatives are in possession of the respondents and as she has been constantly  subjected to various forms of domestic violence, hence the present case.
9. After being served with the notice of the application, the respondents  filed their reply wherein they stated that the aggrieved concealed material facts  misrepresenting the same and had not approached the court with clean hands.

They did not deny the factum of marriage of aggrieved and respondent no.1, 
though, agitated that the respondent no. 2 and 3 are residing separately from  them at D107, JJ Camp, Tigri, New Delhi.

The maintainability of the case has  been challenged due to lack of domestic relationship at the time of filing of  application as also because she is stated to have deserted the respondent no.1  herself.
It has been asserted that the present application has been filed only to  extort money.

All the allegations of the aggrieved in respect of infliction of  domestic violence have been denied and it has been stated that it is aggrieved  who has refused to join the company of the respondent no. 1 and that s herself is earning and is capable for sustaining herself.
Rest of the averments  have been denied on merits.
10. Domestic Incident Report was duly called for and was filed b CC No: 13/1/15 Lalita v Pawan & Ors.

11. After the interim relief application of the aggrieved was decided, parties  were referred for mediation on 17.08.2015 but matter could not be settled there  and it was stated that the respondents were not appearing in media

Thereafter as none appeared on behalf of respondents, respondent no.1 to 3  were proceeded exparte vide order dated 09.03.2016. 
12.
To prove her case, the aggrieved led exparte complainant evidence and  examined only herself to prove her case.

As CW1, the aggrieved Smt. Lalita  tendered her evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. CW1/A) on similar lines as her  application and also relied upon the following documents i.e. copy of her Adhar  Card (Ex.CW1/1), copy of her marriage certificate (Ex.CW1/2A), marriage  Photographs (Ex.CW1/2B), copy of the list of articles (Mark CW1/2), copy of  the settlement before Mahila Panchayat (Mark CW1/3), copy of medical  documents (Ex.CW1/4), copy of complaint filed before CAW Cell in May 2014  Smt. 4 (Ex.CW 1/5), copy of FIR no. 664/14, PS Sangam Vihar (Ex.CW1/6).
13.
I have given my thoughtful consideration to the submissions made on  behalf of the aggrieved during the course of final arguments and have carefully  perused the entire evidence on record.

14. By virtue of Section 2(a), the reliefs under the Protection of Women  From Domestic Violence Act, 2005 can be availed by a woman only if she is in  a domestic relationship with the respondent and was subjected to dom violence by the respondent.

sentences.text:
15. From the unrebutted testimony of CW1 and the documents Ex CW1/2A, 
CC No: 13/1/15 Lalita v Pawan & Ors. Page 5 of  Ex CW1/2B the marriage of the aggrieved with the respondent no.1  13.03.2013 stands duly proved even more so as the same has not been disputed  by the respondents in their reply.
The aggrieved as CW1 has further testified  that thereafter she resided with the respondents at the house of the respondent  no.1 with all the respondents.

Though the respondent no. 2 and 3 took a plea in  their reply as to them residing separately from the aggrieved and the respondent  no.1, as they were proceeded exparte, they failed to defend their case and to  lead any evidence in support of their plea as raised in their defence to prove the  same.
Thus, no rebuttal has come against the claims of the aggrieved.
The oral  testimony of CW1 and has not been traversed and the testimony of CW1 goes  unrebutted and unchallenged.
No reason has been brought on record t disbelieve the unrebutted and uncontroverted evidence led by the aggrieved.
Hence the factum of existence of shared household of the aggrieved and the  respondents
has been proved.

16. In respect of existence of shared household a plea had been raised in the  reply of the respondents that as at the time of filing of the com Smt. Lalita vs Sh. Pawan Kumar on 7 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163182144/
5 aggrieved was not residing under domestic relationship with the respondent, 
hence there was no relationship which was alive at that time hence ingredient remained unfulfilled.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the plea as raised is legall tenable as in the instant case as per the unrebutted testimony of the aggrieved  she was constrained to leave her shared household due to the infli domestic violence by the respondents and not out of her own volition.
Further it  is duly noted that merely because the aggrieved was not living wit CC No: 13/1/15 Lalita v Pawan & Ors.

sentences.text: Pa  respondents at the time of the filing of the application/complaint cannot be said  to result in the domestic relationship ceasing because such restrictiv interpretation if adopted would imply that for the aggrieved to be able to avail  the remedies provided under this Act, she must continue to suffer and reside in  the same place where she is being subjected to violence which is  contrary to the beneficial object of the Act.

17. Further the reliance placed on the judgments by the respondents in their  reply is also misguided for the reason that the judgment of the Hon'ble Delhi  High Court in Harbans Lal Malik v Payal Malik (2010) as also in the case of  Vijay Sharma v State of NCT (2010) are distinguishable as to the facts of the  case.

sentences.text: It is duly noted that as the marriage between the aggrieved has not been  dissolved as on date, the domestic relationship between them cannot be said to  have ceased.
Further as the respondent no.2 and 3 have not led any evidence to  prove that they were residing separately from the aggrieved
, hence it cannot  also not be said that even qua them there was no domestic relationship of the  aggrieved in existence.
Thus from the evidence on record, the domest relationship of the aggrieved with all the three respondents stands duly proved.

18. In respect of the infliction of the domestic violence, the oral testimony  of the aggrieved as CW1 has gone unrebutted as despite opportunities Smt. Lalita vs Sh. Pawan Kumar on 7 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163182144/

. Thu averments of the aggrieved as also her testimony in her evidence by way of  affidavit in respect of infliction of various forms of domestic viol CC No: 13/1/15 Lalita v Pawan & Ors.
Page 7  including physical, verbal and economic abuse are deemed to be admitted by  the respondents as they have remained unchallenged and unrebutted.

Further, 
no reason has been brought on record to disbelieve the uncontroverted evidence  led by the aggrieved.

Accordingly, by unrebutted testimony, the aggrieved has  been able to prove that the respondents have committed certain acts of domestic  violence and as she has been able to prove the domestic violence committed  upon her by the respondents, she is entitled to claim reliefs under the Protection  of Women From Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against all the respondents.

It is pertinent to note that despite seeking a protection order to prohibit  the alienation of jewellery, ornaments and articles including her stridhan, the  aggrieved has not proved the list of articles as relied upon by her as Mark  CW1/B as she did not lead any documentary evidence to prove the same.

Thus, 
in the absence of the list being proved, no protection order as sought by the  aggrieved can be passed.
Hence, this relief for protection order as sought is  declined being vague.
22. Residence Order Under Section 19 of Protection of Women From  Domestic Violence Act:

sentences.text: vi) Direct the respondents to return to the possession of the complainant her  stridhan or any other property or valuable security to which she is entitled to.

23. It is duly noted that in view of the protection orders as already passed  under Section 18 of the Act, no occasion arises for giving further directions as  Smt. Lalita vs Sh. Pawan Kumar on 7 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163182144/
8 sought by the aggrieved regarding any additional conditions or directions to  protect or to provide for her safety or to direct the respondents to execute a  bond, with or without sureties, for preventing the commission of dom violence or for any further directions to the officer in charge of the nearest  police station to give protection.

sentences.text: Hence the reliefs as sought are declined.

24. Further as the aggrieved has not been able to prove which articles of her  stridhan are in the possession of the stridhan nor she has deposed to the nature  of other property or valuable security to which she is entitled, hence the relief  for the same as sought is also declined as being vague and not proved.
25. The aggrieved has also sought alternate accommodation or rent for the
same as also directions against the respondents seeking discharge of rent and
other payments, having regard to the financial needs and resources o parties.
This relief shall however be decided alongwith the monetary relief.
26. Monetary Relief Under Section 20 of Protection of Women From  Domestic Violence Act:

entities.text: Protection of Women From  Domestic Violence Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The aggrieved has sought Rs, 20,000/ per mon towards Food, clothes, medications and other basic necessities; Rs 5,00,000/
towards amount claimed for return of stridhan and damages; Rs 50,000/ for  loss due to removal of belongings from her control for the total  CC No: 13/1/15 Lalita v Pawan & Ors.

27. As per the settled law, the aggrieved is entitled to get monetary relief  which is adequate, fair, reasonable and consistent with the standard of living to  which the aggrieved person is accustomed.

The liability for the same however, 
is primarily that of her husband and cannot be extended to the parents in law of  the aggrieved.

Thus, as it has already been proved that the aggrieved had been  subjected to domestic violence, the respondent no.1 is liable to pay monetary  Smt. Lalita vs Sh. Pawan Kumar on 7 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163182144/
9 relief to the aggrieved.

sentences.text:
28. Now coming to the quantum of maintenance, as per income affidavit of  the aggrieved Lalita, she has studied till class 8th and is unemployed. No assets, 
liabilities or investments have been disclosed by the aggrieved in her income  affidavit though she has claimed household expenses to be about Rs.3000/ and  rent as Rs. 3000/ with medical expenses of Rs 500/.
However no documents  supporting the amounts claimed have been filed or proved by the aggrieved.
29. On the other hand, as per the income affidavit of the respondent no. 1  Pawan Kumar, he has studied till class 5 without any professional qualification  working as a safedi (white wash) worker.
He has not disclosed any member of  his family to be dependent upon him.
He has however, stated his  income to be about Rs. 8000/ per month.
No assets except property D223, JJ  Camp Tigri, New Delhi has been disclosed thought the same is disclosed to be on the name of family members/ HUF.

No liabilities of the respondent have been disclosed in the income affidavit except expenditure of about Rs. 820/ towards electricity,gas etc, Rs. 800 towards conveyance, Rs. 250 towards towards Internet/cable charges, Rs. 3000 towards household expends and Rs. 5000 towards litigation expenses without any other expenses.
He has however, not filed any documents to support his claim of income or expenditure.
30. It is duly noted that in her application the aggrieved has alleged that the respondent no.1 earns about Rs.15,000/ as salary from a private job and has his own house.

She has also stated that the respondent no.1 was the owner of the property at village Katlagudah, Rajasthan however, for reasons best known to her while deposing in the court she has not testified to any such property of the respondent no.1 at Rajasthan.
Further, no documentary evidence has been proved by her as to the job of the respondent no.1 or as to his income therefrom.
Her testimony regarding the immovable property owned by the respondent no.1 is not supported by any documentary evidence.

31. In these circumstances, as the respondent no.1 has himself asserted himself to be a labourer and as the aggrieved is the wife of the respondent no. 1 without any means of sustaining herself, as also keeping in view that it is the legal duty of the respondent no.1 being the husband to maintain her, on the basis of admitted income of the respondent no.1, on the scale of balance of convenience, and in the absence of the respondent having proved the number of family members dependent upon him, it is presumed that only the aggrieved is dependent upon the respondent no. 1 and thus I deem it fit to award a sum of Rs.3500/ per month to the aggrieved by the respondent no.1 towards her maintenance.

Needless to mention that this includes rent towards alternative accommodation because aggrieved despite having a right to reside in the shared household is residing separately Smt. Lalita vs Sh. Pawan Kumar on 7 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163182144/
10 therefrom as also all other ancillary and miscellaneous expenses.

sentences.text: The amount shall be payable to the aggrieved from the date of filing of the petition till the aggrieved becomes disentitled for the same as per law.

32. Respondent no. 1 shall pay the awarded amount directly into the account of the aggrieved upon supplying the details of the bank account within three weeks from today to the respondents and filing a copy on record.
The amount shall be payable by 10th day of every English calendar month starting from the next month.
The arrears be cleared within the period of six months.
33. The default shall be viewed in terms of the judgment of Hon'ble High Court in Gaurav Sondhi Vs. Divya Sondhi-120 DLT(2005)426.

5000/ to be paid by the respondent no.1 to the aggrieved.
35. No grounds exist for granting any other relief in favour of the aggrieved.
36. Application of the aggrieved under Section 12 of the Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is accordingly disposed off in the said terms.
